bull_bear.body: Prioritizing margin enhancement and selective expansion; minimal capex on own stores; focus on franchisee network growth with shared risk; no dividend or buyback mentioned; capital efficiency is core to strategy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Gold price volatility impacting consumer demand; slower-than-expected franchisee onboarding; competition from organized players with aggressive expansion; potential margin compression if diamond mix stalls; execution risk in new small-format store model.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautious, disciplined, and profit-focused; management explicitly avoids revenue-at-all-costs growth; emphasizes selective expansion, profitability over market share, and sustainable returns; confident in margin sustainability and franchise model.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: TBZ’s Vapi store is a test bed for small-format, low-capex franchise units — if successful, this could redefine retail expansion in tier-2 cities without TBZ bearing inventory or rent risk; franchisee model effectively converts fixed costs into variable, improving unit economics.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- 161-year multi-generational legacy and trusted brand heritage in India's organised jewellery sector, currently led by the fifth generation of the promoter family (brand/trust)
- Leadership in the wedding and occasion jewellery segment, contributing approximately 65% of total sales - one of the more resilient demand categories (positioning/demand stability)
- In-house diamond jewellery manufacturing at Kandivali, Mumbai, supporting design exclusivity, quality consistency and margin enhancement (manufacturing/R&D-design)
- Outsourced gold jewellery manufacturing through a network of over 100 vendor partners with regional handcrafted-jewellery expertise, providing scale without in-house capital intensity (cost/distribution)
- Retail scalability: 37 stores across 28 cities in 13 states as of 31 March 2026 (33 large-format, 4 small-format), spanning metropolitan, Tier-I and emerging markets (distribution)
- Early adopter of consumer-trust practices - buyback guarantee since 1938, lightweight jewellery since 1995, and 100% pre-hallmarked jewellery since 2004 - reinforcing brand differentiation (switching/trust)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Macroeconomic risk — Increased geopolitical uncertainty, a potentially slowing global economy, supply-chain disruptions, trade policy changes, tariff shifts, persistent inflationary pressure and heightened gold prices weigh on consumer spending and sentiment, adversely affecting the Company's exports, profitability and growth trajectory.
- Margin risk — Volatile commodity (gold/diamond) prices and fluctuating exchange rates may exert pressure on the Company's margins and overall profitability.
- Competition risk — The gems and jewellery sector faces intense competition from the growing influence of the unorganised sector; any shortfall in delivering high-quality, aesthetically compelling designs could affect market share and expansion prospects versus organised and unorganised peers alike.
- Raw material risk — Any disruption in procuring raw materials (gold, diamonds) on time and at competitive prices could adversely impact operational efficiency and profitability.
- Human capital / attrition risk — The Company explicitly manages employee engagement and training initiatives 'to mitigate attrition,' indicating retention of skilled retail and design staff (workforce of 1,136 as of 31 March 2026) is a monitored risk area.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Gold jewellery dominates at 77% of sales (down from 80% YoY); diamond jewellery share up to 23%; new Vapi store (small-format) performing profitably; franchise model gaining traction with 5-8 active discussions; corporate sales reduced due to low profitability.

business.body: Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri Limited (TBZ - The Original) is a multi-generational Indian jewellery retailer offering gold jewellery, diamond-studded designs and precious gemstone-studded jewellery across festive, wedding and daily-wear segments, with wedding and occasion-related purchases contributing approximately 65% of sales. The Company designs and manufactures diamond jewellery in-house at its Kandivali (Mumbai) facility while gold jewellery manufacturing is largely outsourced to a network of over 100 vendor partners skilled in regional handcrafted jewellery. It retails through its own store network spanning key urban and regional centres across India.

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin up to 12.46% in Q3FY24 (from 11.1% YoY); EBITDA margin expanded to 6.1% (+77 bps YoY); cost discipline in supply chain and reduced low-margin corporate sales driving margin improvement; franchise model shifts retail expenses to partners, improving TBZ’s PBT.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Expect FY25 revenue growth of 15-20% driven by same-store sales growth and franchise expansion; EBITDA margins to sustain above 6.5% with potential upside; no specific revenue target given, but profitability remains core focus.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Franchise expansion to 5-8 new stores by Diwali FY25; potential for small-format store replication in tier-2 cities; margin upside from higher diamond mix and operational efficiencies; possible entry into new geographies via franchisees.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Continue to strengthen domestic presence and expand the retail network in a growth-oriented manner
- Sustain brand relevance and deepen customer engagement through curated, occasion-led marketing campaigns (e.g. festive and wedding-themed IPs)
- Strengthen digital presence through engaging content, video-led storytelling and influencer collaborations to reach younger, tech-savvy consumers
- Introduce new, trend-responsive product lines (e.g. lightweight and detachable jewellery collections) to address evolving consumer preferences
- The Company has formulated a Dividend Distribution Policy (under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations) that pursues the dual objective of rewarding shareholders through dividends while ploughing back earnings to support sustained growth. No investments or divestments were made during the year under review, and the Board recommended a dividend for FY 2025-26.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: TBZ expanded its retail network during FY 2025-26 with two new showrooms — in Ahmedabad, and at Kondapur and Himayatnagar in Hyderabad — taking the total store count to 37 across 28 cities in 13 states. Management's stated outlook is to continue expanding the retail footprint across Indian markets, and as a margin-risk mitigation measure the Company is pursuing network expansion through an asset-light franchise model alongside disciplined cost management and long-term supplier partnerships.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's organised jewellery sector is expected to see approximately 23% revenue growth in FY2025-26, supported by gold's cultural significance, geopolitical-uncertainty-driven investment demand, and the rise of trusted/branded retail formats
- Natural diamond jewellery is emerging as a key growth driver, with India the world's second-largest diamond jewellery market (~12% of global demand); the domestic natural diamond jewellery market, currently valued at approximately Rs 49,700 crore, is projected to reach approximately Rs 1.5 lakh crore by 2030
- Wedding-led demand remains the primary structural driver of gold and jewellery consumption in India, providing a relatively resilient consumption base even amid price volatility
- Consumer preference is shifting towards lightweight, contemporary and branded jewellery, particularly among millennials and Gen Z consumers seeking affordability, modern aesthetics and versatility
- Growing adoption of digital and e-commerce platforms is reshaping jewellery discovery and purchase behaviour, with social media increasingly influencing buying decisions
- Organised/branded retailers are gaining share from unorganised players on the strength of certified products, transparent pricing, exchange and buyback policies, and superior craftsmanship/service standards
- Gold investment demand strengthened materially (ETFs, Sovereign Gold Bonds, Digital Gold) amid sharply rising gold prices, partly offsetting weaker physical jewellery volume demand industry-wide

deepdive.thesis: TBZ is prioritizing profitable margin expansion over revenue growth, successfully increasing EBITDA margins to 6.1% in Q3FY24 through cost discipline and product mix optimization, while strategically deploying franchisees to scale without capital burden. This model enables sustainable growth with minimal capex, positioning TBZ as a high-margin, low-risk player in India’s premium jewellery segment.
